usage: nod — tasks and decisions as plain markdown files A node is one piece of work. If the AI knows how to do it, it is a task; if it needs the owner's answer first, it needs a decision. One kind of thing, one id. nod init create decisions/ in this project nod setup [--for ] wire nod into the coding agent CLIs this project has nod add [flags] new node; -o 1=… 2=… asks the owner, --task makes it a task title ≤ 32 columns (≈16 CJK characters): what to decide, nothing more body can be piped: nod add "T" <<'EOF' … EOF nod get <id> print one node nod show [scope|status] list nodes, one line each (default: needs decision) nod start <id> to do → in progress nod ask <id> -o 1=… 2=… a running node needs the owner → needs decision nod done <id> [--note] → done (archived/) nod add <title> --parent W305 a child node, filed in W305's folder nod add "<a few words>" --brief hand work to an AI (a bare nod add in the owner's own terminal does this) nod claim <id> / expand <id> take a brief, then write its full description nod briefs [--json] briefs nobody has picked up yet, and who is listening nod sessions | session start which AI sessions listen here; open one in a new terminal window nod tree [<id>] [--json] the node tree nod move <id> --parent <id>|--root re-parent a node with its subtree nod supersede <old> --by <new> old → closed (superseded), linked both ways nod search <word>... [--all] titles, bodies, follow-ups, attachment names nod close <id> --reason <r> → closed: superseded | obsolete | merged-into:W15 nod defer <id>... [--off] defer: off the working lists, state kept (--off or undefer to resume) nod push <id> <key> [--note] record your answer (alias: choose) nod queue [--mine] [--stale 1h] answers no agent has collected yet nod read <id>... collect an update from the queue nod archive <id>... file a finished node away nod note <id> <text> [--human] add a note (agent by default); does not archive nod pin <id> [top|bottom|off] order in the bench nod retitle <id> <title> shorten a title (file and id unchanged) nod attach <id> <path|url>... attach a screenshot, file or link nod approved <id> --check <p> does <p> match what was approved? (exit code) nod open <id> [n] open an attachment in the system viewer nod check validate every node nod wait [--mine] block until answered, then exit (for agents) nod changes --since <t> [--mine] everything after t: answers, notes, moves nod monitor [--mine] one line per owner reply or source item — for an agent's Monitor tool nod watch [--mine] stream changes, never exits (for a human's pane) nod source <verb> ... external sources an adapter syncs into nod register/sync/push/heartbeat/list/items/ack/wait/events nod bench [.|<dir>...] the live board; no args = every registered folder nod on a terminal, the same as nod bench; piped, prints this help nod migrate <DECISIONS.md> split a legacy file into decisions/ nod projects [add|rm|list|prune] folders the bench opens from anywhere (~/.decs/config.json) nod config letter W project letter: node 305 shows as W305 nod config lang <code> interface language: en, zh-Hans, zh-Hant, fr, ar nod progress <0-100|--parse …> progress for the node in NODDIT_NODE (pipe-friendly, passes stdin through) nod steps <id> "a" "b" define a node's steps nod step <id> <n> step n done → progress n/total <id> is 305, W305 (project letter W), legacy D305, W:305, or web:305. Common flags: --json --author "<agent> · <doing what>" --dir <project> --lang <code> Environment variables are NODDIT_*; DECS_* names still work too. Run `nod <command> --help` for the rest.

args.flagNeedsTitleAfter: --{{name}} {{value}} must be followed by a title
args.onlyOneDefault: only one option can be the default; you marked {{count}}: {{keys}}
args.defaultMismatch: --default {{explicit}} and default:{{marked}}= do not name the same option
args.subQuestionUndeclared: -o {{key}}= points at sub-question {{qk}}, which was never declared with --question {{qk}} "…"
args.subQuestionMissing: --default {{value}} points at sub-question {{qk}}, which does not exist

context.noDecisionsAbove: no decisions/ in {{path}} or any directory above it
context.noDirHasDecisions: none of the given --dir paths has a decisions/ directory
context.noDecisionsHere:
no decisions/ directory here or in any parent.
Run `nod init` in the project root, or pass --dir <project>.
context.letterClash: project letter {{letter}} belongs to more than one project ({{projects}}) — refer to these by project name instead (e.g. {{example}}:305)
context.noAuthor: who is writing this? pass --author "<agent> · <what it is doing>", or set NODDIT_AUTHOR.
context.otherAuthor: note: {{ref}} was proposed by "{{author}}", not you ({{me}}). Your `nod monitor --mine` will not see its reply — the lead should run monitor without --mine.
context.notYours: {{ref}} was filed by "{{author}}", not you ({{me}}) — check the number. If you really mean to act on it, add --force.

help.approved:
nod approved <id> --check <path>

Checks whether <path>'s current content matches the hash recorded when the
owner approved this node. Run this before sending anything marked with
`nod attach --approval-content` — don't send it if it doesn't match, or
was never approved.

  --json

Exit code: 0 = matches; 2 = this node has no pending attachment matching that
name, it was never approved, or the owner's answer wasn't the approving one;
1 = the content changed since it was approved. The reason goes to stderr (or
--json's reason field).
help.steps:
nod steps <id> "a" "b" "c"          define this node's steps (replaces any existing ones)

Give every step at once; their order is the order they're done in. None
starts out done; nod step <id> <n> marks the first n done and sets the
percentage to n/total.
help.step:
nod step <id> <n>                   steps 1..n are done, percentage set to n/total

  --note "..."   note what this step did (an agent note, recorded in the body)

If there are no steps yet, set them first with nod steps <id> "a" "b" ….
help.progress:
nod progress <0-100> ["msg"]                a one-off set (on the node bound to NODDIT_NODE)
nod progress --parse pytest                             reads "[ 37%]" from stdin, and tees stdin through to stdout unchanged
nod progress --regex '(\d+)/(\d+)'                      a custom regex; converts N/M from stdin into a percentage;
                                                           with only one capture group, it's read as a literal percentage
nod progress --from-file run.log [--parse NAME|--regex R] [--until-exit <pid>] [--idle <ms>]
                                                           follows a growing file (like tail -f);
                                                           waits for that process to exit if --until-exit is given,
                                                           otherwise for --idle ms (default 5000) with no new content
nod progress --count-lines log.txt --total 23            reads the file's current line count once, as count/23 — doesn't follow growth

  --node <id>     reads NODDIT_NODE if not given (NODDIT_TASK also works, the old name); a clear
                  error and non-zero exit if neither is set
  --msg "..."

Built-in parsers (--parse): {{parsers}}; without --parse/--regex, each is tried in turn.
Throttled: writes to the file at most once every 5 seconds per node, but the
last value is always flushed (on process exit or when the file is fully read).
stdin mode works line by line — a progress bar that refreshes in place with
\r and never emits a newline won't be tee'd live; only the line after a
newline is seen.
As soon as a number comes in, a node still "to do" automatically becomes "in
progress" — no need for a separate `nod start` before piping into pytest.
help.move:
nod move <id> --parent <id>     hangs it under another node (with its whole subtree)
nod move <id> --root            makes it a root node

The id stays the same, so every reference still works; the file and its
child-node folder are renamed together, and relative attachment links in
the body are rewritten to match.
help.search:
nod search <word>... [--all] [--json]     find text across nodes

Searches the title, body (including follow-ups, notes, replies) and
attachment filenames, case-insensitively. Every word must appear.
Searches active/ only by default; --all adds archived/ too.
help.supersede:
nod supersede <old id> --by <new id>     old node is superseded by the new one

The old one → closed (reason superseded), filed into archived/, with a note
in its body "superseded by W304"; both sides' front matter record the link
(superseded_by / supersedes), shown both ways by nod get.
help.tree:
nod tree [<id>] [--all] [--json]     the node tree

No id: every tree in active/ (--all adds archived/ too). With an id: the
subtree rooted there. Each line: number · status · title; "waiting on deps"
means it's after unfinished nodes, "◆" means this subtree has something
needing a decision.

  --json   nested structure: { ref, id, status, title, ..., children: [...] }

A child node is created when a lane breaks down its plan:
nod add "<title>" --parent W305. To move it: nod move <id> --parent <id>
or nod move <id> --root.
help.monitor:
nod monitor                run this for Claude Code's Monitor tool — there's only one standard use

  Monitor({ command: "nod monitor", description: "nod", timeout_ms: 1800000 })

  - Arm it as soon as you start working, not only once you're "waiting for an answer".
  - After 30 minutes (or the process exits), **re-arm the exact same command**, with
    no arguments: it remembers where this session last looked, and catches up on
    whatever happened in between.
  - lead / main session: use plain `nod monitor`, **without --mine** (nodes you file
    for a lane are signed with the lane's name).
  - A sub-agent or teammate handles only its own nodes: always `nod monitor --mine`.
    Anything that isn't its own is the lead's.

Each line is one thing to act on:
  - the owner's answer or reply (an agent's own note doesn't count); a node
    pulled back from archive by a reply
  - on startup, every "answered — for AI" node is listed first
  - external-source (nod source) entries that are new or changed
  - DECS-UNCLAIMED …: an answer sitting uncollected for over 5 minutes (regardless of --mine)
  - DECS-BRIEF …: the owner filed a brief — nod claim it, expand, split, nod ask to confirm; once more if still unclaimed after --unclaimed-after (a lead hears every brief, --mine only those under its own nodes)
  - DECS-ERROR …: a read failed; it keeps watching, doesn't exit

  --mine / --author <s>    only one agent's own proposals (by the name before ·) — for a sub-agent only
                           a teammate session (an agent started with --agent-name) gets only its own without it; --all forces everything
  --since <ISO|duration>   start from a given time (rarely needed: defaults to picking up where
                           this session last left off)
  --no-sources             skip external sources
  --unclaimed-after <duration>  default 5m
  --here                   only watch the project under the current directory; exits right away if
                           not inside a nod project (used by the plugin's auto-start)
  --idle-exit <duration>   goes offline on its own after this long with no events (default 2h, 0 = never)
  --interval <ms>          default 2000
  --updates                also a line for every write — an agent's progress, a new or archived node —
                           as DECS-UPDATED <refs> (JSON: event "updated"); for a window that redraws
  --with-parent <pid>      exit when that process is gone (a window that started this monitor)
  --no-heartbeat           don't count as a listening session (a --updates monitor never does)
  --json                   one JSON object per line
help.defer:
nod defer <id>...          deferred: for later, taken off the open/active/needs-decision lists
nod defer <id>... --off    lifts the defer (same as nod undefer <id>...)

Not archiving — it isn't done, just not happening right now. The node's
state (in progress, needs decision, waiting…) doesn't change, and comes
back exactly as it was once lifted. Deferring a parent takes its whole
subtree off the working lists too. Same as pressing d on the bench; the
"Deferred" tab lists every deferred node.

Running it in the owner's own terminal counts as owner (human); inside
Claude Code's shell it's agent — override with --human / --agent. A lane
that sees "owner deferred" should stop and leave it alone until it's lifted.

  --off      lift the defer
  --by <name>  who signs it (defaults to owner / $NODDIT_AUTHOR)
  --json
help.start:
nod start <id>...              the AI starts this node → in progress

  --force   start even if it's still waiting on a decision, or after unfinished nodes
help.done:
nod done <id>... [--note "…"]   it's done → done, filed into archived/

  --note    note what was done (an agent note)
  --force   mark even a node still waiting on a decision as done (rarely right)

Once done, any node after it that was already answered and collected starts automatically.
help.close:
nod close <id>... --reason <reason>   not doing it → closed, filed into archived/

  --reason  superseded | obsolete | merged-into:W15 | any sentence
help.hold:
nod hold <id> --on "<who/what>"     blocked on something external → waiting

Waiting on a colleague, a customer, a vendor, or a service to come back. Not
for waiting on the owner to decide (use nod ask) or on another node (use
--after). A waiting node doesn't count as stuck; resume with nod start.

  nod hold 305 --on "Carol to confirm the invoice amount"
help.ask:
nod ask <id> -o 1="…" 2="…" [--default 1]    partway through, needs the owner to rule → needs decision
nod ask <id>                                  no -o: asks the same question again
                                               (e.g. the owner answered an acceptance node; once it's fixed, ask them to look again)

Once the owner answers, the node becomes "answered — for AI" — it's the AI's
turn, no longer "needs decision". When the AI is done and the owner needs to
look again, nod ask puts it back to needing a decision.

The same node goes back to needing a decision — no new entry. The question's
background comes from stdin or --text; options are written under
`## 选项（第 N 轮）`, with the previous round's options and answer left in
the body as history.

  nod ask 305 -o 1="keep the current CDN" 2="switch to the new one" --default 1 <<'EOF'
  Partway through, the new CDN turned out slower in some regions…
  EOF
help.retitle:
nod retitle <id> "<new title>"     change the title

Title limit {{max}} columns (~{{half}} CJK characters), naming only what to
decide. Only changes front matter's title; the filename and id don't
change, so every reference still works.
help.migrate:
nod migrate — split a legacy DECISIONS.md / DECISIONS.old.md into decisions/

  nod migrate [--dir <project root>] [--dry-run] [--force]
  nod migrate --upgrade [--dry-run]         status: open/answered → node status, written back to file;
                                             an old numbered-list options block (1. label: cost) rewritten as ### 1 · label
  nod migrate --strip-prefix [--dry-run]    D305-….md → 305-….md, attachments/D305 → 305, body links fixed

  --dir <path>   project root to read DECISIONS.md / DECISIONS.old.md from (default: cwd)
  --dry-run      print what would be written, touch nothing
  --force        overwrite an entry file that already exists for that id

Legacy files are never modified or deleted — this only reads them.
help.source:
nod source <verb> ...        external sources: a notification system agents hook into

An AI writes an adapter (usually a background python script polling an
issue tracker / mailbox / feedback form…) that syncs "what's there" into
nod — just id + title (optionally url/state/from), never the body content.
The point is knowing which external sources exist, when they change, and
handling that as it comes in, instead of the owner repeatedly asking "are
issues/mail/feedback all clear?"

For an adapter to use (callable from python via subprocess too):
  nod source register <name> --title "..." [--kind github|mail|feedback|...]
                        [--adapter "python3 ~/…/sync.py"] [--owner-agent "..."]
                        [--stale-after 15m]
  nod source sync <name> < items.jsonl        full snapshot: diffs out new/changed/gone
  nod source push <name> --id X --title "..." [--url] [--state] [--from]
  nod source heartbeat <name>                 just reports it's alive, no data

sync/push's stdin/arguments are the same JSON-lines protocol, one object per line:
  {"id":"123","title":"...", "url":"...", "state":"open", "from":"someone"}
only id/title are required.

For an agent to use:
  nod source list [--json] [--stale]          per source: unhandled count, who's
                                                holding it up, how long since the
                                                heartbeat, whether the adapter looks dead
  nod source items <name> [--unhandled] [--json]
  nod source ack <name> <id>... [--note "..."] [--waiting-on owner|us|<person>|W304]
                                                mark it handled, or record who's holding
                                                it up now (W304 is a node number — nod
                                                now calls decisions and tasks "nodes"
                                                alike, sharing one id space prefixed
                                                with the project letter; a bare D304/304
                                                is also accepted, read as the old style)
  nod source wait [<name>] [--timeout <seconds>] [--json]
                                                blocks until something unhandled is new/changed,
                                                prints it and exits (same philosophy as nod
                                                wait: it doesn't stay running)
  nod source events [<name>] [--since <ISO>] [--json]
                                                changes after since (nod source wait prints a
                                                since cursor on exit)

"Cleared" = no unhandled entries, and nothing is held up on owner/us/an open
node (like W304). Held up on someone else (say Bob) doesn't block cleared —
that's handed off, not still owed by us.
help.attach:
nod attach <id> <path or URL>...

  --link              just record the path, don't copy into decisions/attachments/
  --name              custom link text (only means something when attaching one thing)
  --replace           overwrite the latest version of a same-named file in place, the old
                      version moves into .history/, and links in the body always point
                      at the latest version; without this flag a same-named file becomes
                      name-2.ext and both are kept
  --label "Option 1" a.png --label "Option 2" b.png
                      group the file right after it; the bench lets you flip between
                      files in the same group side by side. Matched to files in order —
                      put one --label in front of each file, no more, no fewer
  --caption "…"       same idea: a one-line caption for the file right after it, shown below the image
  --approval-content  marks this as content that needs your approval before going out;
                      records its sha256. Approve it along with answering the node on
                      the bench, then check it later with `nod approved <id> --check <path>`
  --approve-on 1,3    which answers count as approving this content (comma-separated;
                      a sub-question is written Q2:1). A node with one option (acceptance)
                      defaults to that option; with several options or sub-questions this
                      is required. Any other answer means the content is not approved

Screenshots are copied into decisions/attachments/<id>/ by default, since a
scratchpad gets cleared sooner or later and an acceptance node still needs
looking at next month. Images are written as ![](…), so they just render as
images in any markdown viewer.
help.note:
nod note <id> <text>          append a note; does not answer, does not archive

  --human           this is the owner's own reply (goes on the queue; brings an archived entry back)
  --agent           this is a lane's own note (not queued, wakes nobody)
  --role human|agent
  --author / --by   who signs it; agent defaults to --author / NODDIT_AUTHOR / the branch name, human defaults to owner
  --heading <word>  the section heading; defaults to "Reply" for human, "Note" for agent

With neither --human nor --agent, it goes by who's running it: Claude Code's
shell (CLAUDECODE set) or NODDIT_ROLE=agent counts as agent — records what it
did, adds a fact, **never** queues, never wakes anyone; anything else (the
owner typing in their own terminal) counts as human and goes on the queue.
NODDIT_ROLE=human forces human.

The heading it writes carries the role, signature and time, e.g.:
  ## 补充（agent · lead/ship-v2 · 2026-10-28 10:51:30）
  ## 回复（human · owner · 2026-10-28 11:02:07）
help.archive:
nod archive <id>...        this node is done → done, filed into archived/ (same as nod done)
nod archive <id> --seen    seen it, nothing to do → note that, then archive
nod archive <id> --undo    pull it back into active/

  --force   archive even an entry nobody has answered yet (rarely right)

--seen is for acceptance-style entries: it records "seen, nothing to do",
then archives it, **without queuing it** — the lane that proposed it doesn't
need to be woken for this.

Archiving means "I'm done with it", not "I saw it". For seeing it, use
nod read — it clears it off the queue but leaves it in active/, since the
work isn't finished yet.
help.read:
nod read <id>...        collect these updates (nod pop is the same command)

  --mine / --author <s>   filter check only; the id is still required
  --peek                  look without collecting; stays on the queue
  --done                  collect and archive — this is already settled, or doesn't need settling
  --json

The id is required. There is no "take whatever's at the front of the queue":
with several lanes running at once, grabbing blindly can take someone else's
answer, silently. Look at the queue first, then collect by name:

  nod queue --mine
  nod read 415

**Collecting is not archiving.** read = "I saw it", archive = "I'm done with
it" — these are often days apart. Close it out yourself once it's done:

  nod archive 415

Only use --done when reading it settles it on the spot (e.g. the answer was
"never mind").
help.watch:
nod watch [flags]        runs forever, streaming changes

  --mine / --author <s>   only one proposer's
  --json                  one JSON event per line
  --dir <project>         repeatable

This command **never exits**, so it's meant for a person to watch in a
terminal pane. An agent waiting for an answer should use `nod wait`
instead — that one exits once it gets one, and will wake you if put in a
background shell.
help.changes:
nod changes --since <time> [flags]     everything that happened after it

  --since <ISO|duration>  2026-10-28T10:00:00+08:00, or 2h / 30m (back from now)
  --mine / --author <s>   only one proposer's entries
  --role human|agent      only the owner's / only the agent's
  --json                  { since, until, next_since, events: [...], source_events: [...] }

Lists answers, follow-ups, agent notes, new entries, completions, closures,
reopenings after archiving, and external-source (nod source) entries that
appeared, changed or disappeared. --role only filters nodes, and leaves
sources out when given; --mine / --author filters sources by the
owner_agent they were registered with — a source with none registered is
visible to everyone.

There's no daemon and no event log — everything is derived from entries'
own section headings and front-matter timestamps, so if a session drops or
a wait process is gone, running this once catches up:

  nod changes --since 2026-10-28T10:00:00+08:00 --mine --json

next_since in the output is the --since to pass next time. Older entries'
section headings are only accurate to the minute, so an event within the
same minute may show up twice — better duplicated than missed.
help.wait:
nod wait [<id>...] [flags]        blocks until there's something on the queue, then exits

  --mine / --author <s>   only wait for one proposer's entries
  --timeout <seconds>     exit on timeout, exit code 2; waits forever by default
  --json

It **only tells you "there's an update"**, not what's in it — because you
might answer several at once, and cramming the content into this one exit
would miss the rest. Get the content with nod read:

  nod wait --mine        (run_in_background: true) → wakes you on exit
  nod queue --mine       → see what's there
  nod read <id>          → collect by name (doesn't archive; nod archive once it's done)

On exit it prints a --since value. The wait process disappears with the
session — when you're back, run it once to catch up on every answer and
follow-up from that stretch:

  nod changes --since <the value it printed> --mine

nod watch is the streaming version for a person to watch; that one never exits.
help.push:
nod push <id> <option> [--note "..."]    record your decision
nod push <id> --note "..."               free-text answer when there are no options
nod push <id> Q1=B Q2=1                  a node with sub-questions: answer each one
nod push <id> --defaults [Q2=2]          all defaults, overriding only the ones you write
nod push <id> R3=3:"drop the second paragraph"   pick "change" on one item and say how
(nod choose / nod answer are the same command)

  --note        your own words
  --human       this is the owner's own answer (default follows the shell: agent inside Claude Code)
  --agent       this is an agent recording the answer
  --by          who signs it; human defaults to owner, agent to --author / NODDIT_AUTHOR / the branch name
  --json        the result carries answers: { Q1: "B", … }

Once answered, the node **stays in active/**, state "answered — for AI". A
lane only counts it as picked up once nod read collects it — so if nobody
comes for it, you can still see it in nod queue.

Whoever answers, the answer is recorded and queued the same way; the role
decides exactly one thing — whether content attached with
`nod attach --approval-content` counts as approved: only a human answer
does. When a lead relays what the owner said in a conversation, that's an
agent's answer and approves nothing; anything going out still needs the
owner's own approval, on the bench or in their own terminal.
help.queue:
nod queue [--mine|--author <s>] [--stale <duration>] [--json]

Lists entries you've already answered that no agent has collected yet, oldest
first (FIFO). Read-only — collect with nod read.

  --stale 1h    only list answers older than this, still uncollected (30m / 1h / 2d;
                a bare number is minutes). When an agent gets interrupted and
                forgets to read, these are the answers left hanging.
help.get:
nod get <id> [flags]

  --json        the full machine-readable structure
  --raw         the raw file contents
  --answer      print only the answer (or "open" if unanswered)
  --no-images   don't render screenshots inline
  --cols <n>    how many columns a screenshot gets (default 60, or half the terminal width)

Screenshots are drawn directly in terminals that support it (iTerm2 / WezTerm
via OSC 1337, kitty / Ghostty via kitty graphics). Automatically off inside
tmux — it swallows the escape sequence, and half a picture is worse than none.

The attachment line can also carry: the group a --label put it in (one
heading per line), the "version N" a --replace left behind, and the
approval state from --approval-content (pending / approved / content changed,
needs re-approval).
help.show:
nod show [scope] [--json] [--author <s>] [--stale]

  open        needs a decision — waiting on the owner (default)
  answered    has an answer
  active      everything in active/ (to do, in progress, needs decision, answered — for AI)
  archived    everything in archived/ (done, closed)
  all         everything
  fyi         FYI nodes (just letting you know, no answer needed)
  deferred    deferred nodes (for later; toggle with d on the bench / nod defer)
  <status>    not_started | in_progress | needs_decision | decided | completed | closed

  --stale     only in-progress nodes past their own stale_after (default 30 minutes)
              without an update — put it after the scope: nod show active --stale.
              Defaults to active if no scope is given. Past 2× the threshold it is
              "probably stuck"; --json has a staleness field.

Order: pinned first, then urgency, then deadline, then longest-waiting.
help.add:
nod add <title> [flags]        create a new node (nod send is the same command)

A node is something the AI will do. When the AI knows how, use --task;
when the owner needs to answer a question first, give -o options (needs a decision).
If a problem comes up partway through, use nod ask <id> -o … to turn the same
node into one that needs a decision.

The title is one short phrase, naming only what to decide: at most {{max}} columns
(~{{half}} CJK characters, or about twice that many Latin ones) — anything longer is
rejected outright, since the bench's list view cuts the tail off with "…", and
the cut part is always the half that mattered. Background, numbers and PR
links belong in the body.

  --author, -a  "<agent> · <what it's doing>"   defaults to NODDIT_AUTHOR, then the git branch name
  --option, -o  1="..." 2="..."          repeatable; keys are numbers. Omit it and you get
                                         1="Accepted" — "done, take a look" is
                                         exactly this one-option shape
                default:2="..."          default: before the key marks the default action;
                                         pressing enter on the bench picks it
  --question    Q1 "which CDN?"           a sub-question; its options are -o Q1:A="keep the current one" Q1:B="switch",
                                         give its default as --default Q1:A (every sub-question needs one)
  --review-item R1 "reply to Dave's draft"   one item in a batch review: its options are fixed —
                                         1 pass / 2 fail / 3 change — default 2 (don't send);
                                         the node's own options are generated automatically:
                                         1 all defaults · 2 item by item
  --body        "..."                    or --body-file <path>, or read from stdin
  --default     1                        what happens if you never answer
  --tag         a b c
  --urgency     high | normal | low      default normal; high is pinned to the top in show / bench
  --due         <ISO time | 4h | 2d>     when an answer is needed by
  --if-no-answer "<what I do if you never answer>"   shown directly in bench and nod get
  --reversible  yes | no                 can that default action be undone?
  --fyi                                  just letting you know, no answer needed: left out of
                                         show / wait's "needs decision" list (nod show fyi still sees it)
  --notify                               pushes high-urgency entries: runs $NODDIT_NOTIFY_CMD, with
                                         NODDIT_REF / NODDIT_TITLE etc. in the environment;
                                         does nothing if that variable isn't set
  --task                                 the AI already knows how: no options, state "to do"
  --brief                                the owner hands this to an AI: a few words, expanded and split by whichever
                                         AI session picks it up (nod claim); the words are kept verbatim under 原话.
                                         A bare nod add from the owner's own terminal is a brief; --no-brief opts out
  --parent      W305                     refine: files this as a child node of W305 (into its folder)
  --after       W12 W13                  comes after these nodes (they must finish first)
  --est / --when / --stale-after         estimate, planned time, how long idle counts as stuck — stored, not interpreted
  --json

Piping the body in is the easiest way; a heredoc can write markdown directly:

  nod add "how strict should the deploy gate be" -a "deploy-lane · local deploy path" \
      -o 1="strict: the tree must match exactly" 2="only check files that will ship" --default 1 <<'EOF'
  **What this is.** Now that CI's gate is gone…
  EOF

A whole document can be piped in too — a leading `# Title` line becomes the
title, and a file with YAML front matter (author / default / tags) is read
the same way:

  nod add < entry.md
help.setup:
nod setup [--for claude|codex|kimi|all] [--dir <project>] [--json] [--dry-run]

Wires nod into whichever coding agent CLIs are installed, for one project:
  claude   installs the decs plugin — marketplace then plugin, non-interactively
           when `claude plugin …` allows it; otherwise prints the two lines to
           run inside Claude Code
  codex    adds a decs section to the project's AGENTS.md
  kimi     adds the same section — Kimi reads AGENTS.md too

  --for <id>     only this one (repeatable, or comma-separated); default: all installed
  --dir <path>   project to set up (default: cwd)
  --dry-run      print what would change, write nothing; never runs `claude`
  --json         one machine-readable result, for callers like an onboarding UI

Safe to run again: an agent already wired up reports unchanged. Only the
block between <!-- decs:start --> and <!-- decs:end --> in AGENTS.md is ever touched.
help.claim:
nod claim <id>          take a brief the owner filed, so no other session expands it too

The claim is atomic: it is recorded under the node's lock. A second session
claiming the same brief is refused and told who has it (exit 1). Claiming one
you already hold is a no-op. nod start and nod expand on an unclaimed brief claim it too.

  --force   take over a brief someone else claimed, or claim a node the owner wrote by hand
  --json    `{"ok": true|false, "already": bool, …the node: brief, claimed_by, claimed_at, original}`
help.expand:
nod expand <id> [--title "<title>"] <<'EOF' … EOF
                        write the full description of a brief you picked up

Replaces the description above the `## 原话` section; the owner's words under it,
and every note below, stay as they are. Write what / why / done when, and mark
assumptions as assumptions. Then plan child nodes (--parent, --after, --est) and
nod ask <id> -o 1="start as planned" 2="change it (say how in your reply)".
No work starts before the owner answers 1.

On a node with no 原话 section (a short node the owner wrote), its old
description is moved under one first, so nothing is lost.

  --title     a better title (≤ 32 columns)
  --body / --body-file   instead of stdin
  --json
help.briefs:
nod briefs [--all] [--json]   briefs the owner filed that no AI has picked up, and who is listening

A brief is a node the owner filed with a few words (nod add --brief, or a bare
nod add in the owner's own terminal) for an AI to expand. "Listening" means a
lead session's nod monitor is running in that project; if none is, the brief
waits until one starts.

  --all       also briefs already picked up and not finished
  --project, -p <name>
  --json      `{"projects": [{project, letter, root, listening, listeners: [{author, lead, started_at, at}]}], "briefs": [node…]}`
help.session:
nod sessions [--json]                     which AI sessions are listening, per project
nod session start [--agent claude|codex|kimi] [--dir <project>] [--dry-run] [--json]
                                          open a new terminal window there running that agent

A session is listening when its nod monitor runs in the project (the plugin
starts one in every session). Each monitor keeps a heartbeat under
$NODDIT_HOME/sessions/ (pid, author, harness, lead or sub-agent, started, last
seen); a dead pid or a heartbeat older than 90 seconds doesn't count.

session start opens a new foreground window: iTerm2 if installed, else Terminal
on macOS; Windows Terminal, else cmd, on Windows; the first terminal found on
Linux, else it prints the command. It runs the agent in the project's real root
with a first prompt to pick up the waiting briefs. It refuses when a main
session is already listening there, and says who.

  --agent     claude (default, or $NODDIT_AGENT) | codex | kimi
  --dry-run   print the exact AppleScript / command, open nothing
  --json      sessions: `{"projects": [{project, letter, root, listening, sessions: [{pid, author, harness, role, started_at, last_seen}]}]}`
              start: `{"ok": true, "started": bool, "plan": {agent, root, terminal, command, exec, script?}}`
                     or `{"ok": false, "reason": "already_listening", "session": {…}}`

nod config                      every setting, where its value comes from, and this project's letter
nod config <setting>            one setting's value and where it comes from
nod config <setting> <value>    set it for you (stored in ~/.decs/config.json)
nod config <setting> --off      remove it; back to the default

Settings (an environment variable, where there is one, wins over the stored value; DECS_* names still work too):
{{settings}}

The same settings are in the bench: press , to open them.

lang — {{languages}}. Order: --lang on any command, then NODDIT_LANG, then
nod config lang, then the system locale (LC_ALL / LC_MESSAGES / LANG, or the
OS language), then English.

The project letter tells projects apart when the bench shows several: give
web W and its 305 shows as W305. File names do not change (305-….md; old
D305-….md files still read). A project without a letter shows as {{defaultLetter}}305.
Refs: 305, W305, D305 (old style), W:305 and web:305 all work.
